body_markdown:
In[European (EUR) rates](https://www.tradeweb.com/our-markets/institutional/rates/) , few vanilla post trade workflows are as operationally arduous as trading a swap against a future. It combines an over-the-counter (OTC) product and an exchange-traded derivative (ETD); a venue, an exchange and clearing of both products; and a long post trade operation involving booking and settlement of the listed derivatives. This has meant that trading was built around the phone where pricing revolves around the simple quote of a spread between the two instruments.


In the past two years, that has begun to change. The growth in invoice spreads that we are seeing on Tradeweb suggests one of the large voice bastions in EUR swaps is starting to move, not by replacing the relationships that built the business, but by taking the friction out of the process.


#### A Record Quarter


September was the biggest month on record for EUR Future Spreads on Tradeweb, and Q3 2026 volumes were up 32% on Q2 2026 and 77% on Q3 2025.


The way clients trade is changing too. Average trade size reached a record in Q3 2026, up by 25% on Q2 2026. Clients are no longer testing the protocol with small tickets. They are putting real size through it.


The client mix matters as much as the volume. Activity was spread evenly across real money, hedge funds and bank/prop desks, and when all three segments are active, the shift is structural rather than one-off.


#### The Complexity Behind The Trade


Swaps vs futures is a broad category. They can be traded in a number of ways with the two predominant types being invoice spreads, where the swap matches delivery and maturity dates of the underlying cheapest-to-deliver (CTD) and spot-starting benchmark swaps against the nearest liquid future.


The reason it is an operationally intensive product that crosses multiple teams is due to the nature of the exchange-traded element of the package. The OTC leg is very much rooted in what Tradeweb does, but the listed leg is more complicated as trades have to be booked onto the exchange and often involve different executing brokers, give-up agreements and clearing brokers. In addition, post trade processes can then vary greatly from one client to the next.


This could all make electronification of invoice spreads appear unmanageable. If the liquidity or experience cannot match or improve upon that of dealing on the phone, the benefits of doing so cannot be realised. However, clients want efficiencies, standardised processes and pricing; and the client is behind the push to make this work better.


#### A Decade in the Making


We launched the product in December 2015, and the first trade followed in January 2016, at a time when swaps vs futures was entirely a voice market.


The early years were about laying foundations rather than chasing volume. A product that spans both listed and OTC markets needs infrastructure behind it, so we invested in connectivity to the exchange. This is not possible in some markets, but in EUR we have built a solution that reduces the operational burden, ensuring exchange legs are booked accurately and in a timely manner.


We built alongside clients and dealers throughout, working through how each workflow fits their post trade set-up instead of asking them to adapt to ours. We also kept the product evolving with the market around it, moving on from the original EURIBOR-based launch to introduce invoice spreads referencing ESTR in November 2023.


That groundwork paid off. As dealer participation deepened from late 2023, real usage took hold in 2024, and trade numbers rose more than fourfold in 2025, with 2026 on track to exceed that. Patient investment, close dealer relationships and a focus on getting the workflow right are what put us in a position to deliver when clients were ready to move.


#### Liquidity Is the Turning Point


The real inflection in growth came from depth of liquidity. Bringing more dealers on board creates a stronger marketplace for everyone: clients gain more competition and better pricing opportunities, and dealers gain access to a growing, structured pool of flow.


We now have 14 dealers live for request-for-quote (RFQ), seven of which are also live for request-for-market (RFM). The busiest periods of new dealer onboarding in 2023–24 and again in 2025, line up closely with the strongest volume growth.


RFM matters because of what it protects. It is a two-way request, where a client asks for a market without revealing direction. That has historically been the prevalent way to trade voice, because direction is information and clients are cautious sharing it. There is real demand to trade invoice spreads this way, and since RFM went live in October 2025, backed by the liquidity to support it, it has been one of the key drivers of the growth we are seeing. Clients are protecting their intent, and winning dealers benefit from the same information protection, and they are now doing it electronically.


This demand is reaching real money investors as well as the hedge fund clients. A major sovereign wealth investment firm recently began moving invoice spread business through RFM, a sign that the protocol is credible well beyond early adopters, and that the workflows we have built can flex to varying client needs.


#### The Case for Electronic Execution


The benefits of electronification are familiar across rates, but they are sharper for a product with this much operational weight. Moving the trade onto a single platform brings greater efficiency, fewer manual touchpoints, reduced operational risk, visibility of pricing across multiple dealers and a complete audit trail. For clients, that means a cleaner path to best execution and less time managing the post trade processes.


Dealers benefit too. An invoice spread is a relatively straightforward trade to price, so it fits naturally with automation. That frees sales to spend their time on more complex trades and the conversations that matter most to clients. Straight-through processing (STP) allows dealers to scale, and electronic execution removes the operational risk on the exchange leg.


#### Looking Ahead


Of course, the journey to develop the market’s ability to transact on the platform starts with outrights, but more complex structures and packages of trades will follow and the demand for development within the product space continues to gain momentum.


The size of the opportunity is substantial, with daily average volumes reported by the exchange in this product sitting at nearly €15 million in delta. We are working on bringing swaps and futures into multi-asset package (MAP) workflows and on packages of different swaps and futures combinations. With record activity, larger trade sizes, a balanced client base and growing dealer depth, we are well placed to keep the momentum building.
